scope: GTK2 native multiline TextView: Motif word-wrap behavior, four KDE schemes, normal/disabled/backdrop states, coupled/separate previews, editing and scroll behavior

reference.version: local Theme Lab Motif sample; not the SR10.4 VM
reference.caveat: The isolated Motif screenshot is grayscale under Xvfb and does not validate the historical VM palette/font. The shown widget bounds are a 97x54 px crop from the local sample.

implementation.change: The real GTK2 TextView in the native comparison scene now uses Gtk.WrapMode.WORD before inserting the sample text, matching XmNwordWrap=True. GTK theme colors remain generated from KDE View/Selection roles; no final RGB was added.

checked: native TextView wrap mode is WORD in every scene
short sample has no horizontal scrollbar
long multiline sample scrolls vertically without a horizontal scrollbar
effective KDE View role matches sampled track pixels in all schemes and states
coupled and separate allocation, sensitivity, font description and sample text
transactional scene rebuild preserves UTF-8 text and preview Undo/Redo
editing-only pass: Ctrl+A/C/X/Z/Y/Shift+Z with multiline UTF-8 in both origins
verification.environment_note: GTK emitted the existing ATK bridge module warning under Xvfb; assertions completed successfully.

visual_comparison.result: Word wrapping now matches the Motif control and removes horizontal scrolling. At the 97x54 crop, GTK2 still displays a vertical scrollbar and clips the last word because its 13px preview font needs more height/width than the local Motif sample. No arbitrary per-control font reduction was introduced.

limitations: This is a local Motif sample comparison, not a measurement or visual acceptance of Domain/OS SR10.4.
The Motif Xvfb capture is grayscale; color fidelity is not claimed from that image.
At the matching crop size, font metrics leave one vertical scrollbar and clipped text in GTK2; the preview retains the KDE-derived 13px font rather than hard-coding a smaller size.
